    27	  syntax Val ::= closureValC(ParamNames, ParamNames, Stmts, Map)
    28	
    29	  // capture: resolve each freevar to the enclosing frame's cellRef, then bind
    30	  // (FuncDef) or yield (Lambda) the closure value.
    31	  syntax KItem ::= #mkClosure(String, ParamNames, ParamNames, ParamNames, Stmts, Map)
    32	                 | #mkLambda(ParamNames, ParamNames, ParamNames, Stmts, Map)
    33	  rule <k> FuncDef(F:String, Params(PNS:ParamNames), CellVars(CVS:ParamNames),
    34	                   FreeVars(FVS:ParamNames), BODY:Stmts)
    35	        => #mkClosure(F, PNS, CVS, FVS, BODY, .Map) ... </k>
    36	  rule <k> #mkClosure(F:String, PNS:ParamNames, CVS:ParamNames,
    37	                      (FV:String, FVR:ParamNames), BODY:Stmts, CM:Map)
    38	        => #mkClosure(F, PNS, CVS, FVR, BODY, CM [ FV <- {M[FV]}:>Val ]) ... </k>
    39	       <env> L:Int </env>
    40	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, _) ... </scopes>
    41	       requires FV in_keys(M)
    42	  rule <k> #mkClosure(F:String, PNS:ParamNames, CVS:ParamNames,
    43	                      .ParamNames, BODY:Stmts, CM:Map) => .K ... </k>
    44	       <env> L:Int </env>
    45	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map => M [ F <- closureValC(PNS, CVS, BODY, CM) ], _) ... </scopes>
    46	
    47	  rule <k> Lambda(Params(PNS:ParamNames), E:Expr)
    48	        => closureVal(PNS, Return(E) .Stmts, L) ... </k>
    49	       <env> L:Int </env>
    50	  rule <k> Lambda(Params(PNS:ParamNames), CellVars(CVS:ParamNames),
    51	                  FreeVars(FVS:ParamNames), E:Expr)
    52	        => #mkLambda(PNS, CVS, FVS, Return(E) .Stmts, .Map) ... </k>
    53	  rule <k> #mkLambda(PNS:ParamNames, CVS:ParamNames,
    54	                     (FV:String, FVR:ParamNames), BODY:Stmts, CM:Map)
    55	        => #mkLambda(PNS, CVS, FVR, BODY, CM [ FV <- {M[FV]}:>Val ]) ... </k>
    56	       <env> L:Int </env>
    57	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, _) ... </scopes>
    58	       requires FV in_keys(M)
    59	  rule <k> #mkLambda(PNS:ParamNames, CVS:ParamNames, .ParamNames, BODY:Stmts, CM:Map)
    60	        => closureValC(PNS, CVS, BODY, CM) ... </k>
    61	
    62	  // ==== bind params ========================================================
    63	  rule <k> #bindP(.ParamNames, .Vals) => .K ... </k>
    64	  rule <k> #bindP((P:String, PS:ParamNames), (V:Val, VS:Vals)) => #bindP(PS, VS) ... </k>
    65	       <env> L:Int </env>
    66	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map => M [ P <- V ], _) ... </scopes>
    67	  // a param that is a cellvar was pre-bound to its cell at frame entry
    68	  rule <k> #bindP((P:String, PS:ParamNames), (V:Val, VS:Vals))
    69	        => #cellW({M[P]}:>Val, V) ~> #bindP(PS, VS) ... </k>
    70	       <env> L:Int </env>
    71	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, _) ... </scopes>
    72	       requires "$cells" in_keys(M)
    73	        andBool pnMember(P, cellsOf({M["$cells"]}:>Val))
    74	        andBool P in_keys(M) andBool isCellRef({M[P]}:>Val)
    75	       [priority(40)]
    76	
    77	  // ==== return / pop the frame (the returned expr evaluates by strictness) ==
    78	  rule <k> Return(V:Val) ~> _ => #pop </k>
    79	       <ret> noRet => retV(V) </ret>
    80	  rule <k> #endcall => #pop ... </k>
    81	       <ret> noRet => retV(noneV) </ret>
    82	  // pop: restore env, DEALLOCATE the callee frame, and wind scopeLoc back (LIFO allocation
    83	  // makes the saved loc the callee frame's own loc). Sound because no closureVal outlives its
    84	  // defining frame (frontend subset: no returned/stored closures; module defs live in loc 0).
    85	  rule <k> #pop => V ~> CONT </k>
    86	       <ret>   retV(V) => noRet </ret>
    87	       <stack> ListItem(frame(CONT:K, CALLERL:Int, SAVEDL:Int)) => .List ... </stack>
    88	       <env>   L:Int => CALLERL </env>
    89	       <scopes> SC:Map => SC [ L <- undef ] </scopes>
    90	       <scopeLoc> _ => SAVEDL </scopeLoc>
    91	endmodule
     1	// reference/src/semantics/str.k — MPY-STR
     2	
     3	module MPY-STR
     4	  imports MPY-CORE
     5	  imports MPY-ITER
     6	
     7	  // ==== iteration (the iterator protocol's str case; yields 1-char strings) ==
     8	  rule <k> #iterNext(str(.IntSeq))                 => #iterDone ... </k>
     9	  rule <k> #iterNext(str(iCons(C:Int, R:IntSeq)))
    10	        => #iterYield(str(iCons(C, .IntSeq)), str(R)) ... </k>
    11	
    12	  // ==== str literal (ASCII-only) ============================================
    13	  syntax IntSeq ::= strToCodes(String) [function]
    14	  rule <k> Str(S:String) => str(strToCodes(S)) ... </k>
    15	  rule strToCodes("") => .IntSeq
    16	  rule strToCodes(S:String) => iCons(ordChar(substrString(S, 0, 1)), strToCodes(substrString(S, 1, lengthString(S))))
    17	    requires S =/=String "" andBool ordChar(substrString(S, 0, 1)) <Int 128
    18	
    19	  // ==== operators: + / == / != / in =========================================
    20	  syntax IntSeq ::= seqConcat(IntSeq, IntSeq) [function, total]
    21	  rule seqConcat(.IntSeq, T:IntSeq)                => T
    22	  rule seqConcat(iCons(I:Int, S:IntSeq), T:IntSeq) => iCons(I, seqConcat(S, T))
    23	
    24	  rule applyBin("+",  str(A:IntSeq), str(B:IntSeq)) => str(seqConcat(A, B))
    25	  rule applyCmp("==", str(A:IntSeq), str(B:IntSeq)) => A ==K B
    26	  rule applyCmp("!=", str(A:IntSeq), str(B:IntSeq)) => notBool (A ==K B)
    27	
    28	  // substring membership: `P in X` iff the code-seq P occurs contiguously in X
    29	  rule applyCmp("in",     str(P:IntSeq), str(X:IntSeq)) => strContains(P, X)
    30	  rule applyCmp("not in", str(P:IntSeq), str(X:IntSeq)) => notBool strContains(P, X)
    31	
    32	  syntax Bool ::= strPrefix(IntSeq, IntSeq) [function, total]
    33	  rule strPrefix(.IntSeq, _:IntSeq)               => true
    34	  rule strPrefix(iCons(_:Int, _:IntSeq), .IntSeq) => false
    35	  rule strPrefix(iCons(A:Int, As:IntSeq), iCons(B:Int, Bs:IntSeq)) => A ==Int B andBool strPrefix(As, Bs)
    36	
    37	  syntax Bool ::= strContains(IntSeq, IntSeq) [function, total]
    38	  rule strContains(P:IntSeq, X:IntSeq) => true  requires strPrefix(P, X)
    39	  rule strContains(P:IntSeq, .IntSeq)  => false requires notBool strPrefix(P, .IntSeq)
    40	  rule strContains(P:IntSeq, iCons(C:Int, Xs:IntSeq)) => strContains(P, Xs)
    41	       requires notBool strPrefix(P, iCons(C, Xs))
    42	
    43	  // ==== lexicographic order: < / <= / > / >= by code point (= Python str order on the code
    44	  // model). strLt reduces on GROUND code-seqs (krun) but is inert/OPAQUE on symbolic ones
    45	  // (a proof's codesProj(V) is an abstract IntSeq — no constructor rule matches), so a symbolic
    46	  // str `<` stays a trusted opaque term the way sortVS / intFloatDiv do. Additive: fires only on
    47	  // str </<=/>/>= comparisons.
    48	  syntax Bool ::= strLt(IntSeq, IntSeq) [function, total]
    49	  rule strLt(.IntSeq, .IntSeq)                => false
    50	  rule strLt(.IntSeq, iCons(_:Int, _:IntSeq)) => true
    51	  rule strLt(iCons(_:Int, _:IntSeq), .IntSeq) => false
    52	  rule strLt(iCons(A:Int, As:IntSeq), iCons(B:Int, Bs:IntSeq)) => true          requires A  <Int B
    53	  rule strLt(iCons(A:Int, As:IntSeq), iCons(B:Int, Bs:IntSeq)) => false         requires A  >Int B
    54	  rule strLt(iCons(A:Int, As:IntSeq), iCons(B:Int, Bs:IntSeq)) => strLt(As, Bs) requires A ==Int B
    55	
    56	  rule applyCmp("<",  str(A:IntSeq), str(B:IntSeq)) => strLt(A, B)
    57	  rule applyCmp(">",  str(A:IntSeq), str(B:IntSeq)) => strLt(B, A)
    58	  rule applyCmp("<=", str(A:IntSeq), str(B:IntSeq)) => notBool strLt(B, A)
    59	  rule applyCmp(">=", str(A:IntSeq), str(B:IntSeq)) => notBool strLt(A, B)
    60	endmodule
     1	// reference/src/semantics/concrete.k — MPY-CONCRETE
     2	// Concrete-execution-only rules, visible ONLY to the llvm build (run.sh kompiles
     3	// MPY-CONCRETE; verification builds import MPY and never see these). Rationale:
     4	// a k-cell rule matching value constructors NARROWS abstract Vals in the haskell
     5	// backend ([concrete] is not respected on rewrite rules) — probed on
     6	// 26-remove-duplicates, where element compares branched into deepEqVS.
     7	
     8	module MPY-CONCRETE
     9	  imports MPY
    10	
    11	  // deep equality for list compares whose elements are heap objects
    12	  // (list-of-lists): Python == is structural at every depth.
    13	  rule <k> Compare(list(A:ValSeq), CmpOp("==", list(B:ValSeq))) => deepEqVS(A, B, HP) ... </k>
    14	       <heap> HP:Map </heap>
    15	       requires hasRefVS(A) orBool hasRefVS(B)
    16	  rule <k> Compare(list(A:ValSeq), CmpOp("!=", list(B:ValSeq))) => notBool deepEqVS(A, B, HP) ... </k>
    17	       <heap> HP:Map </heap>
    18	       requires hasRefVS(A) orBool hasRefVS(B)
    19	
    20	  // ==== keyed sort, concrete leg ============================================
    21	  // Computes each key by a REAL call through the uniform #callee machinery
    22	  // (closures, len, type objects all work), stable-inserts on the key, and
    23	  // allocates the result. priority(40) beats sort.k's opaque rules, so krun
    24	  // runs this and proofs (which never see MPY-CONCRETE) keep sortKeyVS.
    25	  syntax Val ::= kvP(Val, Val)
    26	  syntax KItem ::= #ksort(ValSeq, Val, ValSeq, Bool)
    27	                 | #ksIns(Val, ValSeq, Val, ValSeq, Bool)
    28	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("sorted")), (list(VS:ValSeq), kwV("key", KV:Val), .Vals))
    29	        => #ksort(VS, KV, .ValSeq, false) ... </k>
    30	       [priority(40)]
    31	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("sorted")), (list(VS:ValSeq), kwV("key", KV:Val), kwV("reverse", RB:Bool), .Vals))
    32	        => #ksort(VS, KV, .ValSeq, RB) ... </k>
    33	       [priority(40)]
    34	  rule <k> #ksort(.ValSeq, _:Val, ACC:ValSeq, RB:Bool)
    35	        => #alloc(list(condRev(unpairVS(ACC), RB))) ... </k>
    36	  rule <k> #ksort(vCons(V:Val, R:ValSeq), KV:Val, ACC:ValSeq, RB:Bool)
    37	        => KV ~> #callee((V, .Exprs)) ~> #ksIns(V, R, KV, ACC, RB) ... </k>
    38	  rule <k> K:Val ~> #ksIns(V:Val, R:ValSeq, KV:Val, ACC:ValSeq, RB:Bool)
    39	        => #ksort(R, KV, insPair(ACC, K, V), RB) ... </k>
    40	       requires notBool isKwV(K)
    41	
    42	  syntax ValSeq ::= insPair(ValSeq, Val, Val) [function]
    43	  rule insPair(.ValSeq, K:Val, V:Val) => vCons(kvP(K, V), .ValSeq)
    44	  rule insPair(vCons(kvP(K2:Val, V2:Val), R:ValSeq), K:Val, V:Val)
    45	    => vCons(kvP(K, V), vCons(kvP(K2, V2), R))
    46	       requires kLt(K, K2)
    47	  rule insPair(vCons(kvP(K2:Val, V2:Val), R:ValSeq), K:Val, V:Val)
    48	    => vCons(kvP(K2, V2), insPair(R, K, V))
    49	       requires notBool kLt(K, K2)
    50	
    51	  syntax Bool ::= kLt(Val, Val) [function]
    52	  rule kLt(I1:Int, I2:Int)             => I1 <Int I2
    53	  rule kLt(F1:Float, F2:Float)         => F1 <Float F2
    54	  rule kLt(str(A:IntSeq), str(B:IntSeq)) => strLt(A, B)
    55	  // v3: mixed Int/Float keys via the exact v2 bridges (float.k), bool keys by
    56	  // the bool->int promotion (True==1, False==0). Unordered pairs (int vs str)
    57	  // stay without a leg — stuck, like CPython's TypeError.
    58	  rule kLt(I:Int, F:Float)   => ltIF(I, F)
    59	  rule kLt(F:Float, I:Int)   => ltFI(F, I)
    60	  rule kLt(B:Bool, V:Val)    => kLt(boolAsInt(B), V) requires isInt(V) orBool isFloat(V)
    61	  rule kLt(V:Val, B:Bool)    => kLt(V, boolAsInt(B)) requires isInt(V) orBool isFloat(V)
    62	  rule kLt(B1:Bool, B2:Bool) => boolAsInt(B1) <Int boolAsInt(B2)
    63	
    64	  syntax ValSeq ::= unpairVS(ValSeq) [function, total]
    65	  rule unpairVS(.ValSeq) => .ValSeq
    66	  rule unpairVS(vCons(kvP(_:Val, V:Val), R:ValSeq)) => vCons(V, unpairVS(R))
    67	  rule unpairVS(vCons(V:Val, R:ValSeq)) => vCons(V, unpairVS(R)) [owise]
    68	
    69	  // ==== non-keyed reverse sorted(), concrete leg (v3) =======================
    70	  // sort.k's condRev(sortVS(VS), true) reverses equal-key runs — invisible on
    71	  // the all-Int / all-str lists sortVS used to accept, visible once sortVS
    72	  // orders mixed numerics (CPython keeps FIRST-seen order among equal keys
    73	  // under reverse=True). rev-in/rev-out over the same stable ascending sortVS
    74	  // is exactly CPython's stable descending sort, and is output-identical on the
    75	  // old homogeneous domains. krun-only (priority 40; proofs keep sort.k's
    76	  // condRev(sortVS(VS), RB) term unchanged).
    77	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("sorted")), (list(VS:ValSeq), kwV("reverse", true), .Vals))
    78	        => #alloc(list(revVS(sortVS(revVS(VS))))) ... </k>
    79	       [priority(40)]
    80	
    81	  // ==== numeric cross-type membership (Python: 1 == True == 1.0) =============
    82	  // `x in list` / `x not in list` compare elements with ==K in list.k, which does
    83	  // NOT collapse across the numeric types (true =/=K 1, 1 =/=K 1.0). Under krun,
    84	  // override the membership fold with a numeric-aware equality so `in` and
    85	  // unique()-style dedup behave like CPython for mixed int/bool/float elements.
    86	  // (set.k needs no change: setV holds int char codes, compared with ==Int, so a
    87	  // cross-type ==K collapse never arises there.)
    88	  // krun-only (priority 40 beats list.k's default rules); kprove uses the
    89	  // structural ==K rules in list.k unchanged.
    90	  syntax Bool ::= numOrKEq(Val, Val) [function]
    91	  rule numOrKEq(A:Val, B:Val) => applyCmp("==", A, B)
    92	       requires (isInt(A) orBool isBool(A) orBool isFloat(A))
    93	        andBool (isInt(B) orBool isBool(B) orBool isFloat(B))
    94	  rule numOrKEq(A:Val, B:Val) => A ==K B [owise]
    95	
    96	  rule <k> #iterYield(E:Val, _:Iterable) ~> #memberCont(V:Val) => true ... </k>
    97	       requires numOrKEq(E, V) [priority(40)]
    98	  rule <k> #iterYield(E:Val, R:Iterable) ~> #memberCont(V:Val) => #memberAcc(V, R) ... </k>
    99	       requires notBool numOrKEq(E, V) [priority(40)]
   100	endmodule
     1	// reference/src/semantics/bool.k — MPY-BOOL
     2	// Bool operator cases + the truthy boolean operations (not / and / or; and-or are
     3	// value-returning short-circuit over any Vals, per Python).
     4	
     5	module MPY-BOOL
     6	  imports MPY-CORE
     7	
     8	  rule applyUn("not", V:Val) => notBool truthy(V)
     9	
    10	  rule applyCmp("==", B1:Bool, B2:Bool) => B1 ==Bool B2
    11	  rule applyCmp("!=", B1:Bool, B2:Bool) => B1 =/=Bool B2
    12	
    13	  // bool is a subtype of int: a Bool compared with an Int promotes to 0/1 and
    14	  // re-dispatches to the Int comparison cases (True==1, False==0, True<2, ...).
    15	  // The == / != Bool x Bool cases above are kept; only the four ordering ops are
    16	  // promoted for Bool x Bool (to avoid duplicating the two rules above).
    17	  rule applyCmp(OP:String, B:Bool, I:Int) => applyCmp(OP, boolAsInt(B), I)
    18	       requires isEqOrdOp(OP)
    19	  rule applyCmp(OP:String, I:Int, B:Bool) => applyCmp(OP, I, boolAsInt(B))
    20	       requires isEqOrdOp(OP)
    21	  rule applyCmp(OP:String, B1:Bool, B2:Bool) => applyCmp(OP, boolAsInt(B1), boolAsInt(B2))
    22	       requires isOrdOp(OP)
    23	
    24	  // ==== BoolOp: short-circuit, value-returning and / or =====================
    25	  // the node is its own accumulator: heat the HEAD element only, then either return it
    26	  // (short-circuit) or drop it and continue
    27	  context BoolOp(_, (HOLE:Expr, _:Exprs))
    28	  rule <k> BoolOp(_:String, (V:Val, .Exprs)) => V ... </k>
    29	  rule <k> BoolOp("and", (V:Val, A:Expr, REST:Exprs)) => BoolOp("and", (A, REST)) ... </k>
    30	       requires truthy(V)
    31	  rule <k> BoolOp("and", (V:Val, _:Expr, _:Exprs)) => V ... </k>
    32	       requires notBool truthy(V)
    33	  rule <k> BoolOp("or",  (V:Val, _:Expr, _:Exprs)) => V ... </k>
    34	       requires truthy(V)
    35	  rule <k> BoolOp("or",  (V:Val, A:Expr, REST:Exprs)) => BoolOp("or", (A, REST)) ... </k>
    36	       requires notBool truthy(V)
    37	
    38	  // ==== heap-object head: decide truthiness THROUGH the heap, never rewrite the
    39	  // operand — and/or return the OBJECT itself (Python identity), not its structure
    40	  rule <k> BoolOp(_:String, (ref(H:Int), .Exprs)) => ref(H) ... </k>
    41	       [priority(40)]
    42	  rule <k> BoolOp("and", (ref(H:Int), A:Expr, REST:Exprs)) => BoolOp("and", (A, REST)) ... </k>
    43	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    44	       requires truthy(V)
    45	       [priority(40)]
    46	  rule <k> BoolOp("and", (ref(H:Int), _:Expr, _:Exprs)) => ref(H) ... </k>
    47	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    48	       requires notBool truthy(V)
    49	       [priority(40)]
    50	  rule <k> BoolOp("or", (ref(H:Int), _:Expr, _:Exprs)) => ref(H) ... </k>
    51	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    52	       requires truthy(V)
    53	       [priority(40)]
    54	  rule <k> BoolOp("or", (ref(H:Int), A:Expr, REST:Exprs)) => BoolOp("or", (A, REST)) ... </k>
    55	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    56	       requires notBool truthy(V)
    57	       [priority(40)]
    58	endmodule
     1	// reference/src/semantics/int.k — MPY-INT
     2	// Int cases of the operator dispatch; Python // and % are floored (pyMod).
     3	
     4	module MPY-INT
     5	  imports MPY-CORE
     6	
     7	  rule applyUn("-", I:Int) => 0 -Int I
     8	
     9	  rule applyBin("+",  I1:Int, I2:Int) => I1 +Int I2
    10	  // Bool participates in int arithmetic (x += (a == b))
    11	  rule applyBin("+",  I:Int, B:Bool) => I +Int #if B #then 1 #else 0 #fi
    12	  rule applyBin("+",  B:Bool, I:Int) => #if B #then 1 #else 0 #fi +Int I
    13	  // bool is a subtype of int: any Bool operand promotes to 0/1 and re-dispatches
    14	  // to the Int cases (the "+" mixed cases above are kept, so "+" is excluded here
    15	  // to avoid a duplicate rule — Bool + Bool still promotes via the Bool x Bool rule).
    16	  rule applyBin(OP:String, B1:Bool, B2:Bool) => applyBin(OP, boolAsInt(B1), boolAsInt(B2))
    17	       requires isArithOp(OP)
    18	  rule applyBin(OP:String, B:Bool, I:Int)    => applyBin(OP, boolAsInt(B), I)
    19	       requires isArithOp(OP) andBool OP =/=String "+"
    20	  rule applyBin(OP:String, I:Int, B:Bool)    => applyBin(OP, I, boolAsInt(B))
    21	       requires isArithOp(OP) andBool OP =/=String "+"
    22	  rule applyBin("-",  I1:Int, I2:Int) => I1 -Int I2
    23	  rule applyBin("*",  I1:Int, I2:Int) => I1 *Int I2
    24	  rule applyBin("%",  I1:Int, I2:Int) => pyMod(I1, I2)
    25	  rule applyBin("//", I1:Int, I2:Int) => (I1 -Int pyMod(I1, I2)) /Int I2
    26	  rule applyBin("**", I1:Int, I2:Int) => I1 ^Int I2 requires I2 >=Int 0
    27	
    28	  syntax Int ::= pyMod(Int, Int) [function]
    29	  rule pyMod(I1:Int, I2:Int) => ((I1 %Int I2) +Int I2) %Int I2
    30	
    31	  rule applyCmp("<",  I1:Int, I2:Int)   => I1 <Int  I2
    32	  rule applyCmp("<=", I1:Int, I2:Int)   => I1 <=Int I2
    33	  rule applyCmp(">",  I1:Int, I2:Int)   => I1 >Int  I2
    34	  rule applyCmp(">=", I1:Int, I2:Int)   => I1 >=Int I2
    35	  rule applyCmp("==", I1:Int, I2:Int)   => I1 ==Int I2
    36	  rule applyCmp("!=", I1:Int, I2:Int)   => I1 =/=Int I2
    37	endmodule
